items.title: Rail fares frozen for a second year, ministers confirm
items.description: Passengers will see no increase in regulated fares next March after a decision announced in Parliament. Operators said the freeze would be funded through savings on timetable changes. Campaign groups welcomed the news but called for simpler ticketing.

items.title: Storm Eleanor brings travel disruption to western coasts
items.description: Gusts of up to 70mph are expected overnight with flooding likely in low lying areas. Ferry services have been suspended and several rail routes are running reduced timetables. Residents are advised to check local alerts before travelling.

items.title: Library visits rise for the third year running
items.description: Public libraries recorded their busiest year since 2015, with children events and free computer access cited as the main draws. Councils say funding remains tight, and some branches still operate shortened hours.

items.title: Scientists map hidden valleys beneath Antarctic ice
items.description: A new radar survey has revealed a network of ancient river valleys buried under the ice sheet. Researchers say the data will help predict how quickly the ice moves towards the sea.

items.title: Local bakery wins national bread award
items.description: A family run bakery from Shropshire took the top prize for its slow fermented sourdough. The owners said the award came after a difficult year of rising ingredient costs.

items.title: Heritage groups call for restoration of 1930s lido
items.description: Campaigners have launched a petition to bring the disused lido back into use. A feasibility study suggests the pool could reopen within three years if funding is secured.

items.title: Energy prices to fall slightly from January
items.description: The regulator has announced a small fall in the price cap for the winter quarter. Analysts warned that bills would remain well above levels seen before 2021.

items.title: Hospital trial uses robots to move supplies overnight
items.description: Autonomous carts now deliver linen and medicines between wards at a London hospital. Staff said the pilot freed nurses for patient care and will be reviewed in the spring.

items.title: Film festival opens with restored silent classic
items.description: Organisers unveiled a newly restored print of a 1927 horror film, accompanied by a live orchestra. Tickets for the week long festival sold out within hours.

items.title: Council to plant 10,000 trees along city cycle routes
items.description: The planting scheme aims to cool streets in summer and absorb traffic noise. Volunteers will be recruited through local schools and community groups.
